Module 4. Digital Commerce, Social Media and Intelligent Customer
Systems
1. E-Business:
Definition:
E-business is the use of internet and digital technologies to run any part of an organisation's
operations - buying, selling, customer service, internal processes, and collaboration with
partners - not just online buying and selling.
Diagram:
Fig: Scope of E-Business
Explanation:
E-business is the umbrella term: it covers everything from internal systems like ERP and HR,
to customer support, to collaborating digitally with suppliers, with e-commerce being just one
part of it - the part that deals specifically with online transactions.
Advantages / Benefits:
• Wider scope of efficiency: Digitises entire operations, not just sales, cutting cost and
delay across every department.
• Better integration: Connects customer-facing and internal processes onto shared
digital systems.
Dhrupesh Sir | SBIS Module 4 Notes

slides.text:
Fig: B2B - Business Selling to Business
Explanation:
A B2B transaction usually flows through procurement portals or B2B marketplaces: the
buying business places a purchase order, the supplying business ships the goods, and payment
is settled between the two companies, often with negotiated pricing and longer sales cycles
than a typical consumer purchase.
Advantages / Benefits:
• Large order values: Bulk transactions mean higher revenue per sale than typical
consumer orders.
• Recurring relationships: B2B buyers often become long-term, repeat customers.
• Streamlined procurement: Digital portals speed up ordering, invoicing, and
reordering.
Disadvantages / Limitations:
• Longer sales cycles: Negotiation and approval steps make B2B deals slower to close.
• Complex integration needs: Buyers often expect the portal to connect with their own
ERP or procurement systems.
• Smaller customer base: Fewer potential buyers exist compared with the mass market
in B2C.
Examples:
• Example 1: A car manufacturer ordering steel sheets in bulk from a supplier via a B2B
portal.
• Example 2: A wholesaler selling stock to multiple retailers through IndiaMART or
Alibaba B2B.
Dhrupesh Sir | SBIS Module 4 Notes

3. B2C (Business-to-Consumer):
Definition:
B2C (business-to-consumer) e-commerce is when a business sells products or services directly
to individual end customers, typically through an online store or app.
Diagram:
Fig: B2C - Business Selling to Consumer
Explanation:
In a B2C transaction, the business lists products online, the consumer browses and purchases
directly, and payment is completed digitally - the most familiar and widely used form of e￾commerce, emphasising an easy browsing and checkout experience for a large, diverse
customer base.
Advantages / Benefits:
• Huge customer reach: A single store can reach millions of individual consumers
online.
• Convenient shopping: Customers can browse and buy anytime, from anywhere.
• Rich customer data: Every browse and purchase generates data to improve marketing
and offers.
Disadvantages / Limitations: Dhrupesh Sir | SBIS Module 4 Notes

Since buyer and seller are typically strangers, the platform plays a central trust role: it hosts the
listing, handles or escrows payment, and provides a ratings or review system so both parties
can trust the transaction.
Advantages / Benefits:
• Low barrier to sell: Anyone can list an item without setting up a business.
• Good value for buyers: Used or handmade goods are often cheaper than buying new.
• Built-in trust tools: Ratings and reviews help strangers transact safely.
Disadvantages / Limitations:
• Trust risk: Fraud or misrepresented items remain a real risk between strangers.
• Inconsistent quality: No standard quality control since sellers are individuals, not
businesses.
• Dispute handling burden: The platform must resolve disagreements between buyer
and seller.
Examples:
• Example 1: Someone selling a used smartphone to another individual on an online
marketplace.
• Example 2: A crafter selling handmade jewellery directly to buyers on Etsy.
Applications:
• Resale marketplaces: Selling used goods between individuals.
• Classifieds platforms: Listing items for local pickup or sale.
• Handmade goods marketplaces: Independent sellers reaching individual buyers.

slides.text:
Fig: Mobile Commerce - Categories and Transaction Flow
Explanation:
M-commerce uses mobile-specific capabilities such as GPS, push notifications, and biometric
login to let customers shop, compare, and pay from anywhere, spanning categories like
shopping, banking, ticketing, and location-based services.
Advantages / Benefits:
• Convenience: Customers can buy anytime, anywhere, without needing a computer.
• Location personalisation: Apps can use GPS to offer nearby deals or local delivery.
• Fast checkout: Saved cards and biometric login make payment quicker than desktop
entry.
Disadvantages / Limitations:
• Small-screen limits: Limited space restricts how much detail can be shown per product.
• Device security risk: Lost phones or unsecured Wi-Fi add extra attack surface.
• Platform fragmentation: Separate iOS, Android, and web builds increase
development cost.
Examples:
• Example 1: Ordering groceries via an app and paying instantly through a mobile wallet.
Dhrupesh Sir | SBIS Module 4 Notes

6. Digital Payment Systems:
Definition:
Digital payment systems are electronic mechanisms - cards, wallets, and bank transfers - that
move money between buyer and seller without physical cash, underpinning virtually all e￾commerce.
Diagram:
Fig: Digital Payment Systems - Transaction Flow
Explanation:
A payment gateway, processor, and issuing/acquiring banks work together to authorise and
settle a transaction within seconds, using encryption and tokenisation to protect card details
throughout.
Advantages / Benefits:
• Speed: Payments settle in seconds instead of days. Dhrupesh Sir | SBIS Module 4 Notes

Explanation:
Businesses use social platforms for marketing, feedback, and community-building, supported

costs.
• Real-time feedback: Comments and reviews give instant visibility into customer
sentiment.
• Organic virality: Good content can be shared widely by users at no extra cost.
Disadvantages / Limitations:
• Reputational risk: Negative content can spread just as fast as positive content.
• Moderation burden: Requires ongoing effort to manage inappropriate or false content.
• Algorithm dependency: Organic reach depends on platform algorithms outside the
business's control.
Examples:

Explanation:
A CRM consolidates data from every touchpoint into one customer profile, and is generally
split into operational (day-to-day sales/support automation), analytical (data-driven insight),
and collaborative (cross-department data sharing) functions.

slides.text:
Fig: AI Chatbot / Virtual Assistant Architecture
Explanation:
A chatbot pipeline turns user input into an intent (NLU), tracks conversation context, consults
a knowledge base or API for the answer, and generates a natural-language reply (NLG) back to
the user, repeating the loop each turn.
Advantages / Benefits:
• 24x7 availability: Responds to queries instantly at any hour.
• Scalability: Handles thousands of conversations simultaneously.
• Cost reduction: Automates routine queries, freeing human agents for complex issues.
Disadvantages / Limitations:
• Limited emotional handling: Struggles with nuanced or emotionally sensitive queries.
• Misunderstanding risk: Poorly trained models can misinterpret intent.
• Setup cost: Requires investment in training data and ongoing refinement.
Examples:
• Example 1: A website chatbot instantly answering 'Where is my order?' by checking the
logistics system.
• Example 2: A banking assistant letting a customer check balance or transfer funds by
typing a request.
Applications:
• Customer support: Automating FAQs and order tracking. Dhrupesh Sir | SBIS Module 4 Notes

10. Digital Marketing Analytics:
Definition:
Digital marketing analytics is the practice of collecting and analysing data from digital
channels to evaluate campaign performance and guide marketing decisions.
Diagram:
Fig: Digital Marketing Analytics Pipeline
Explanation:
Data from website, social, email, and ad channels is tracked, processed into KPIs and
dashboards, and interpreted through a funnel (awareness, interest, conversion, loyalty) to see
where customers convert or drop off.
Advantages / Benefits:
• Measurable ROI: Every marketing spend can be traced to clicks, leads, and sales.
• Real-time optimisation: Underperforming campaigns can be adjusted quickly.
• Granular targeting: Reveals exactly which segments and channels perform best.
Disadvantages / Limitations:
• Data fragmentation: Combining data across many platforms is technically difficult. Dhrupesh Sir | SBIS Module 4 Notes

11. Recommendation Systems (Amazon, Netflix and Similar Platforms):
A recommendation system analyses past user behaviour - purchases, ratings, views - to predict
and suggest items a user is likely to want, personalising the experience for each individual.

slides.text:
Content-based filtering matches items to a user's own past preferences, while collaborative
filtering matches users with similar behaviour to each other; most large platforms combine
both into a hybrid engine that ranks final suggestions.
Advantages / Benefits:
• Increased sales/engagement: Relevant suggestions drive additional purchases or
watch time.
• Better discovery: Surfaces niche items a user might otherwise never find.
• Automatic personalisation: Scales individually tailored suggestions to millions of
users.
Disadvantages / Limitations:
• Cold-start problem: Hard to recommend well for new users or new items with no
history.
• Filter bubble: Can over-narrow variety by repeating similar suggestions.
• Popularity bias: Tends to favour already-popular items over new ones.
Examples:
• Example 1: Amazon showing 'customers who bought this also bought' suggestions.
• Example 2: Netflix showing a personalised homepage that differs per subscriber.
Applications:
• E-commerce: Suggesting related or complementary products.
• Streaming: Personalising watch/listen recommendations.
• Advertising: Targeting ads based on predicted interest.

slides.text:
Fig: Case Study Comparison - Amazon, Netflix and Flipkart/Alibaba
Explanation:
Amazon combines B2C/B2B marketplace with collaborative-filtering recommendations and
strong logistics; Netflix relies on subscription video with a hybrid recommender driving most
viewing; Flipkart and Alibaba show large-scale marketplaces adapted to local logistics and
payment needs.
Advantages / Benefits:
• Practical insight: Shows how theory translates into real competitive advantage.
• Benchmarking: Gives newer businesses proven patterns to learn from.
• Regional adaptation lessons: Shows how strategy must adapt to local markets.
Disadvantages / Limitations:
• Limited transferability: Strategies at massive scale may not suit smaller businesses.
• Quick to date: Fast-changing platforms make case details go stale quickly.
• Survivorship bias: Only successes are studied, not the many similar failures.
Examples:
• Example 1: Amazon Prime bundling delivery and streaming to build customer lock-in.
• Example 2: Flipkart scaling infrastructure massively for its annual sale event.
Applications:
• Strategy education: Teaching real applications of digital-commerce concepts. Dhrupesh Sir | SBIS Module 4 Notes
